boundaries.contract: `cmd_Protocol` is a `ConfCmdFn` stored as `SslConfCmdTbl.cmd` by the private `commands()` table (`src/ssl/ssl_conf.rs:922`, row `:998`). The only indirect invocation is `f(cctx, value)` in `SSL_CONF_cmd` (`:1426`), reached from `SSL_CONF_cmd_argv` (`:1459` -> `:1505`). `SSL_CONF_cmd_value_type` (`:1532`) reads only `value_type`, never `.cmd`. Preconditions: (1) `cctx` is non-NULL, aligned, live, initialised, and exclusively accessible: `SSL_CONF_cmd` rejects a NULL `cctx`/`cmd` at `:1398`; provenance is one zeroed `size_of::<SslConfCtx>()` block from `SSL_CONF_CTX_new` (`:1561`); `SSL_CONF_CTX_set_ssl`/`_set_ssl_ctx` (`:1684`/`:1728`) set `ctx`/`ssl` to NULL or live in-crate objects; the shared `&*cctx` at `:1410` is used only for lookup and ends (NLL) before `:1426`, so the handler's writes do not alias a live shared borrow. (2) `value` is non-NULL and NUL-terminated: `SSL_CONF_cmd` rejects NULL for a typed row at `:1419`; NUL-termination is the public caller contract at `:1368`. (3) No retention of `value`: the handler passes it to `parse_option_list`, which stores only the frame-local flag table in `cctx.tbl` and clears `tbl`/`ntbl` before returning (`:498-499`). (4) Return: `CONF_parse_list` gives 1 when an element matched and 0 otherwise; `SSL_CONF_cmd` maps >0 to 2 and every other value to 0. (5) NULL `cctx` is never delivered (dispatch guard); if it were, the handler would dereference it. A NULL `value` is not delivered either; the handler would answer 0 (CONF_parse_list's NULL arm). (6) Error path: `cctx.tbl`/`ntbl` are cleared on every path; `CONF_parse_list` has its own `guard_ffi`. The slot is private; exclusivity is now a stated precondition of the public SSL_CONF_cmd (# Safety :1368, B46-D1), whose authority documentation states neither (see preconditions).

It does not prove NUL-termination of an arbitrary caller buffer (that is the caller's contract), only that the handler consumes the literal up to its terminator.
